title: Calcitriol and myelin in WOREE
summary: A conditional comparator for testing glial vitamin D receptor (VDR) function.

graph.hypothesis: Glial VDR could help deficient axons.

evidence: A rat OPC marker increased at 50–100 nM after stripped-serum conditioning. Conventional-serum cultures showed no detectable increase.
inference: At 50 nM, the nominal culture concentration was about 430 times the total serum peak measured in children on dialysis. Juvenile neural free exposure is unknown.
hypothesis: A glial VDR response could support first sheaths even on Wwox-deficient axons. Increased MBP alone can coexist with a lasting axonal deficit.
experiment: Qualify local calcitriol measurement. Compare first stable sheaths per eligible axon and conduction across axon and glial genotypes, with glial VDR, precursor reserves and minerals controlled.
limits: Adult brain assay sensitivity depends on input mass. Clinical experience concerns renal and endocrine disease. Pediatric WWOX study priority is deferred.
